source.title: Global convergence of ResNets: From finite to infinite width using linear parameterization
source.authors: Raphaël Barboni; Gabriel Peyré; François-Xavier Vialard

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including the numerical experiments and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training outcomes for a finite-width ResNet-like model on CIFAR-10, using empirical risk rather than training classification error.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-10 training curves are figure-only. The paper also states the model can reach almost zero loss, but does not give a CIFAR-10 value in text. Comparisons and claims about cited prior work are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study establishes convergence guarantees for specially parameterized residual networks and reports training cross-entropy on CIFAR-10. It does not report training classification error from random initialization, compare plain networks with residual networks, or isolate the initialization, normalization, or stability effects named in V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the experimental claims, but omits the main theoretical conclusion: conditional linear convergence of GD for RKHS-NODEs, retained at sufficiently large finite width. The authors state that experiments reach almost zero loss and that fixed-hidden-layer residuals perform similarly to trained-hidden-layer variants. Their theoretical guarantees concern full-batch GD; extension to SGD is left open.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a modified ResNet18-inspired architecture with simplified residual blocks, removed batch normalization and final nonlinearities, fixed hidden convolutions for RKHS residuals, zero initialization of trained convolutions, and SGD with batches. This differs from the claim versions' standard classification training recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: NODE block depth (1, 10, or 20 layers) changes reported performance; 10 and 20 layers are described as very similar.

fits_no_version.finding: Modified CIFAR-10 residual networks with fixed or trained hidden convolutions achieve similar performance; 10 and 20 NODE-block layers improve training performance over one layer and perform similarly to each other.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth and fixed-feature residual parameterization affect training cross-entropy in modified ResNet18 architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Under regularity, expressivity, embedding, width, and step-size conditions, full-batch GD converges to zero loss in the RKHS-NODE model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suitably constructed continuous-depth residual networks admit conditional global convergence guarantees.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST, four input channels produce substantially poorer empirical-risk convergence than eight or 32 channels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing the embedding dimension can improve optimization of RKHS-NODEs.

record.problems: CIFAR-10 training-risk curves are figure-only in the supplied text, so exact values cannot be extracted. The stated test accuracies do not establish training classification error. Results average 20 runs; the reported CIFAR-10 comparison is against the authors' SHL variant and original ResNet18 test accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Figure 3 also reports test classification error, but the text gives only selected test-accuracy statements; those do not measure the training-error outcome in V1.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 from random initialization, including label corruption and the stated capacity and training-recipe qualifications.
Spurious-minimum frequencies and the effect of one or two extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation in plain networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts; the specified tanh and Fixup extensions.
Comparisons of activation-matched initializations, signal or gradient preservation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate sweeps relative to the initial stability threshold, curvature dynamics, recovery, and divergence.
Controlled comparisons of normalization versus no normalization for training speed, learning-rate tolerance, or Fixup-equivalent stability.

record.verdict_notes: Near-zero cross-entropy could bound training classification error, but the supplied text provides neither numerical CIFAR-10 endpoints nor an explicit training-error result. The general almost-zero-loss statement does not establish V1 under its specified initialization conditions. Fixup-like initialization and removal of normalization are recipe choices here, not controlled tests of V4 or V6.

versions.untested_parts: No corrupted or random labels, smaller-model comparison, early stopping, or regularized recipe is tested. The reported CIFAR-10 measure is empirical risk, not training classification error.

rows.subject: RKHS residuals
rows.size_stated: ResNet18-inspired architecture; arbitrary D residual layers in the NODE block; channel count not stated for CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD on CIFAR-10; hidden convolutions fixed and shared as RKHS residuals; W convolutions initialized at 0.
rows.uncertainty: Plots are averages over 20 runs; colored areas show mean ± one standard deviation.
rows.note: Figure-only curve; the paper says 1 layer achieves 82% test accuracy with RKHS residuals, which is not the training measure.
rows.check: Training cross-entropy is not the training classification error specified in V1; the supplied figure text contains no readable curve values. Trained W convolutions start at zero.
